title: India court orders release of 'Cockroach' party leaders as movement calls for fresh protests. Follow DW
summary: Leaders of the youth-led protest movement were detained ahead of a large demonstration in Delhi demanding India's election commissioner step down. Meanwhile, fresh protests have been called. Follow…

image.caption: Parts of Delhi were locked down Saturday with a mammoth deployment of police and paramilitary personnel,Image: Abiraj Kumar Arulgnanakumar/DW

blocks.text: What is the latest on the protests?
The CJP is set to hold a press conference in New Delhi at 2 p.m. local time (8.30 am UTC) today, the group said Sunday.
Meanwhile, it is yet to be seen if a fresh protest in New Delhi will take place. On Saturday evening, temporary protest leader Ajinkya Shinde had called for new demonstrations.
Earlier on X, Shinde said that a protest was scheduled in Mumbai at 4 p.m. adding that more cities "will follow."
As of early afternoon in Delhi, there were no signs of any major gathering of protesters around the Jantar Mantar site in the center of the city.
On Saturday, Mumbai too saw a series of detentions at a protest against the chief election commissioner over alleged electoral roll irregularities.

According to reports, around 600 protesters were detained and later released. The detainees included Tushar Gandhi, the great-grandson of India's independence icon Mahatma Gandhi, and Bollywood actor Imran Khan.
